newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates flat, Mideast sees ULCC fixture.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates flat, Mideast sees ULCC fixture.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were mostly steady on Monday amid a flurry of Middle Eastern fixtures for ultra large crude carriers (ULCCS) including the world's largest ship, the 550,000-tonne Jahre Viking.
"There has been a bit of a mad rush on ULCCs but the VLCC market has quietened down a bit," one London-based broker said.
Rates for VLCCS were similar to Friday's levels amid average chartering, and dealers saw these ships at W55 for Mideast/ Singapore routes, as well as for routes west from the Mideast.
Japanese destinations were worth about five points more, brokers said.
"There has been no surge in (Mideast) rates yet although I expect we will see more of a rush next week as we see the December stems coming in," one said.

West African markets were quieter than last week, in a two-tier market, with older 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes fetching around W87.5 for destinations in the U.S. Gulf and newer vessels worth around five points more.
Rates to Europe from West Africa were assessed as being broadly comparable with those to the U.S. Gulf.

Med rates were also little changed, with cross-Med Suezmax routes valued between W85 and W95. These were lower than fixtures seen on Friday out of Novorossiisk, but those were above market because of the extra expense attached to that port.
Cross-Med routes for 80,000 tonne Aframaxes were fetching around W105. A fixture at W101 was below market because of the short ballast time, brokers said.
Aframax rates for Inter/U.K.Cont routes were valued at a wide 95-107.5, with a surplus of old ships depressing the lower end of the range. But business was quiet.
Bad weather in the North Sea, and a dearth of million-barrel vessels there, were expected to push up rates soon. -- Nicholas Shaxson, London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
